thread:
louise: Heads-up: after turning on prefix-caching for beta tenants we saw batch-size oscillation and a spike in KV evictions. I want to capture design decisions for the scheduler to address jitter without regressing throughput.

ben: Do we think it's admission instability (clients re-trying) or internal coalescer churn? Initial traces show a lot of small batches being cut ~30ms apart.

louise: Traces indicate both. Clients that used to hit a warm shard now cause a small batch, then another small batch when kv rehydration completes. The scheduler's watermark is too aggressive.

tara: Proposal: introduce a probabilistic soft-hold window after a batch cut that prefers coalescing more requests into the same cut if the shard shows high locality. Call it `soft_hold_ms` with decay per-shard.

jordan: I like soft-hold, but it can increase tail latency for low-locality tenants. Need a per-tenant SLA knob or a deadline override from the API.

louise: Agree. API-level deadline must win. Also we can make `soft_hold_ms` adaptive: low when deadlines are tight, larger when many requests show the same `prefix_hint`.

ben: Scheduler bookkeeping: we'll need a cheap hot-counter per shard that decays exponentially. Counter++ on admit hit, decrement via decay tick. Use that to bias coalesce decisions.

tara: Also consider an admission probe: allow transient admit with flag `probe=true` that doesn't reserve KV bytes but still records hit/miss to build a heatmap. If probes become hot we promote them to full admit. This avoids pre-allocating memory for noisy tenants.

jordan: That solves conservative pre-reservation, but how do we avoid double work when a probe triggers a follow-up full admit? We might duplicate decoding work.

louise: We can short-circuit probes: if probe finds KV warm and another request arrives within `fast_follow_ms` we fold it into a promoted full admit instead of redoing work. That requires a lock on the shard warm state. Cheap optimistic CAS should work.

ben: Telemetry gap: current metrics don't attribute eviction pressure to shard locality. Let's add `redwood_kv_lease_bytes_total{shard}`, `redwood_kv_probe_promotions_total`, and traces with `shard_heat_score`. Also emit a compact per-batch event: `batch_cut{shard, batch_size, hold_ms, deadline_warning}`.

tara: For rollout: 1) start by emitting metrics only and enabling `soft_hold` off by default. 2) Canary `probe=true` for 2% of traffic, collect promotions and duplicate-work rate. 3) Enable `soft_hold` for low-SLA tenants and measure tail latency.

jordan: Backcompat: add a compat-layer in front of SDKs that maps `enqueue()` to `claim_slot({prefix_hint, deadline_ms, probe:false})`. The new name helps us avoid confusion in code. We'll expose `probe:true` in experimental SDKs only.

louise: Tests: simulate a tenant with bursty arrivals that shrink to warm-hot pattern and measure batch oscillation metric. Also simulate memory pressure where promoted probes lead to eviction cascades.

ben: Eviction strategy: prefer evicting entries with low shard_heat_score and low recency. Add an eviction budget threshold `evict_until_percent=60` so we don't thrash around 100% memory. Use tiny hysteresis windows.

tara: Runbook: if `redwood_kv_probe_promotions_total` >> baseline and `redwood_batch_oscillation_ratio` rises, steps: 1) flip compat proxy to probe-only for the tenant, 2) raise `soft_hold_ms` for that shard, 3) consider marking tenant as "no-prefetch" for 1 hour.

jordan: One more item: quantized model variation. If model memory footprint changes at runtime (A/B kernels), probes must include `kernel_profile` so we can promote to correct reservation class. Otherwise we under/over-commit.

louise: Good catch. Add `kernel_profile` to probe and admit events.

probe-bot: Canary summary report: probe traffic 2% (tenants: 12) over 1h: promotion rate 4.1%, duplicate-work 0.6%, batch_oscillation_ratio decreased 18% for canary tenants.

louise: Nice. Next steps: draft RFC follow-up with the `soft_hold` algo, `probe` contract, metric names, and canary checklist. @ben take the probe proxy, @tara add metrics + runbook edits, @jordan add tests + kernel_profile plumbing. We'll review tomorrow.
